bio.short: Tyler Nichols is a long jumper and high jumper for Texas from Clinton, Mississippi. In 2026 he set the Sun Belt long jump record at 8.19m, won both jumps at the conference meet and became a two-time All-American. He was a 2026 Project Manager Intern at Feniex Industries.
long: Nichols competes in two very different events, the long jump and the high jump, and in 2026 he won both at the Sun Belt Outdoor Championships for Southern Miss. His long jump of 8.19m (26 feet 10.5 inches) broke an 11-year-old conference record and was then the second-best mark in NCAA Division I; he cleared 2.18m to take the high jump. That year he earned USTFCCCA Second-Team All-America honors twice in the long jump: ninth at the NCAA Indoor Championships and 14th at the NCAA Outdoor Championships in Eugene.

He grew up in Clinton, Mississippi, and started competing in track and field at 13. At Clinton High School he won the MHSAA Class 6A high jump title in 2021 and 2022, and his 6-10 clearance in 2022 ranked No. 1 in the state. He spent three seasons at Southern Miss, where his long jump reached a conference-record 8.19m in 2026, before transferring to Texas for his senior year. His Texas bio says he chose Texas because he loves Texas. He studies Physical Culture & Sports, and away from the track he paints and draws.

Nichols is direct about his standard. "Second best, first loser," he told WDAM before the 2026 NCAA meet, crediting an upbringing that taught him to be better than he was yesterday. Contesting two events at the same championship means planning warm-ups, attempts and recovery across a multi-day schedule, a discipline that carried over to his 2026 Project Manager Internship at Feniex Industries, the Austin manufacturer of emergency-vehicle lighting, sirens and controllers, where he supported project coordination across teams.

inTheirWords.quote: Being second, that's my only motivation, honestly. Second best, first loser, that's what I like to say.
I don't like being second. I don't like being anything other than first.
I've always been taught to be first, be the best, be better than yourself, better than what you were yesterday.
